card.name: Auxiliary verbs before passive outcomes
card.fires_on: Auxiliary or linking words (be, is, are, been, was, could) that follow a subject and come right before a passive verb about something being affected, lost, augmented or nurtured.

modes.label: Auxiliary before passive
modes.description: A form of 'be' after a subject, where a passive verb of effect is expected next.
modes.example: all the hard-fought progress made by so many to restore the Great Lakes could<< be>> lost, he said in written statement accompanying

modes.label: Drug effect statements
modes.description: The verb 'is' after a drug effect, before 'augmented' or similar.
modes.example: The antihypertensive effect of enalapril<< is>> augmented by antihypertensive agents

modes.label: Other linking words
modes.description: Words like 'but', 'that' or 'power' after a subject, where an affected-by verb may follow.
modes.example: already-unionized<< but>> increasingly militant teachers in Chicago.

card.writes: It pushes toward words meaning 'suffer', 'be subjected to' or 'be hit by', mostly Chinese ones, such as 遭到 and 受到.
card.plain: It fires on small verbs like 'is' or 'be' when the sentence is about to say something was affected, lost or changed by something.
